correctness.rationale: At integer r>=2 and any finite n>=1,k,m>=0, if two agents differ in large-good counts by >=2, transfer one heavy good and optimally redistribute their combined unit goods. The attainable pair-load differences have fixed parity and centers r Delta and r(Delta-2)>=0; lowering center cannot raise minimum achievable absolute imbalance, and therefore improves global majorization. Sum of squared heavy-good counts strictly falls, proving termination at counts q or q+1. With fixed balanced baselines, assigning each unit item to currently least-loaded agent minimizes every convex separable sum by ordered marginal increments; same vector therefore is majorized by every feasible allocation. Explicit three-case compressed formula follows by water-filling baselines with gap r. For noninteger r>1, select two agents, two large items and odd integer m with |2r-m|<1: balanced heavy items give discrepancy 1, whereas putting both heavy on one agent and units on the other gives smaller discrepancy, so the two-stage rule is not universally Lorenz optimal. Independent brute-force enumerated all labeled allocations and verified sorted partial sums for n=2–4 representative heavy/light multiplicities, including n=4,k=3,m=3,r=3 with 4096 assignments. All stated boundaries include zero items and one agent. Not an impossibility claim for any other allocation method at irrational ratios.

originality.rationale: Common-object Lorenz domination for all symmetric Schur-concave welfare functions is stronger than maximizing a single p-mean objective, whereas the established 2026 algorithms and 2022 bivalued papers target Nash, leximin, or egalitarian objectives individually. Their algorithmic implications do not automatically prove the every-convex-sum majorization minimality or iff integrality for the named two-stage algorithm. General identical-machine two-job-length scheduling and resource-allocation literature are substantial prior-coverage risks; the present structural smoothing lemma and compressed exact profile were not located as an existing corollary in inspected material. Treat best-of-knowledge rather than absolute priority.
residual_risks: Older two-job-length scheduling / convex load-balancing theorems, especially McCormick et al. 2001, might imply all-objective dominance and require detailed specialist comparison.
The theorem covers common normalized valuations, not general heterogeneous two-type Nash or arbitrary positive sizes.
Explicit total Nash product can have huge output; the optimal profile is in compressed multiplicity form.

value.rationale: For identical valuations this is a motivated complete characterization of a canonical allocation policy across *all* symmetric Schur-concave objectives, with a sharp arithmetic distinction integer versus noninteger ratios. The explicit three-case load multiset uses O(1) integer divisions even when multiplicities are binary-encoded, while the counterexample shows why the rule breaks outside its sharp boundary. This is an independently useful allocation and majorization theorem, beyond solving one utility objective.
